category_title: Verbal students with HFA who struggle with environmental distractions and role ambiguity
minimal_context: The student and her partner are preparing to collaborate on a temple-building task in an OpenSim-based virtual environment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to start the temple-building task in the virtual environment. You and A need to work together on this.

STUDENT: I am very excited to use the OpenSim environment! Where is A? We should walk or fly to the building area together.

TUTOR: A is over on the other island right now. Go ahead and get started.

STUDENT: (Takes the initiative to transport A to the gathering place) Okay, A is here now. We are ready to start our design work.

TUTOR: A is asking who should lead the temple-building task. What do you want to tell A?

STUDENT: I don ’t really know. I am gonna like what you gonna do.

options.A: Disable the voice chat function at the start of the temple-building task and enable it as needed later.
options.B: Establish a balance between collaboration and individualization as a precept for the design partnership during the temple-building task.
options.C: Use the symbols 'O' and 'X' rather than long aural or textual descriptions during the temple-building task.
options.D: Revise the Behavioral Intervention Plan to include specific strategies for preventing escape attempts during the temple-building task.
